transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-05-28 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~46 minutes
- Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood SE), Grace (Orion Head of Platform), Tom (Orion CISO), Ellen (Orion DevOps)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood Console and API focused on data handling and retention controls: live demo of logging redaction, PII detection rules, request storage toggles, per-route retention policies, and KMS integration. Discussed enterprise security needs and next steps for a POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Avery from Redwood, i'll hand off to Samir and Lina to do the demo but quick introductions?
[00:06] Grace: Hi all, Grace here, head of platform at Orion. We're particularly interested in how you can keep PII out of logs and also the retention controls because our compliance team requires 90-day retention for certain logs and immediate deletion on request.
[00:14] Tom: Tom Reyes, CISO. Main concerns: audit trail, KMS integration, and proof we aren't sending cardholder data to third parties.
[00:21] Ellen: Ellen, DevOps, i'll be implementing any VPC or network stuff.
[00:25] Avery: Great, quick agenda — show Console features, API toggles, then some Optimize suggestions around batching and what that means for logs, then Q&A and next steps. Samir, Lina?
[00:32] Samir: Yep thanks. We'll jump in; first question for you Grace, what's your current flow today — are you calling hosted APIs, or do you have an in-house inference stack?
[00:39] Grace: Right now it's a mix; we use a managed LLM API for non-sensitive calls, but all card data and anything tied to payments goes to our internal models. We're evaluating Redwood for routing and for cost/latency predictability and more importantly data controls.
[00:51] Samir: Understood. Two quick clarifications: (1) Do you need private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or would Redwood Hosted with enhanced controls suffice for initial POC? (2) do you have specific encryption/KMS provider — AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM?
[01:02] Grace: POC can be hosted if we can demonstrate the retention toggles and redaction. For KMS we primarily use AWS KMS, but we might need HSM options later.
[01:10] Samir: Good. We'll demo the hosted flow with KMS key integration and show the private option in the scoping.
[01:15] Lina: Jumping into the Console — i'm sharing my screen — this is the Routes page, you can see a per-route retention policy. For this customer we have a toggle labeled "Request storage" — by default on, but you can flip it off so the raw request payload never persists. If you keep it on you can choose retention days, and apply redaction rules.
[01:31] [Samir clicks]
[01:34] Samir: Note: when request storage is off, we still emit aggregate metrics and token-level cost but not the content. So billing and latency metrics are preserved.
[01:42] Grace: Wait so if we turn request storage off will we still be able to replay requests for debugging?
[01:46] Lina: No — with storage off the full request body is not stored. We offer structured logs and a scrubbed metadata view for debugging: timestamps, model ID, route, tokens, and error codes. For debugging you can enable temporary session logging for a limited time window with an explicit audit entry and admin approval.
[02:00] Tom: How does redaction work — is it before storing or after? And is it deterministic? We need to show auditors that card numbers are never stored.
[02:08] Samir: Redaction happens inline during ingestion — pre-storage. We have built-in PII detectors (emails, credit card patterns, SSNs, phone numbers) plus a custom rule engine where you can add regex or key-value path masks for structured JSON payloads. It's deterministic for standard detectors; custom rules depend on the expression you provide.
[02:22] Ellen: Any false positives/negatives concerns? Our traffic includes tokenized fields and sometimes numbers that look like cc numbers.
[02:28] Lina: You can tune sensitivity and add allowlists/denylists. Also we provide a "preview" mode on redaction rules so you can run them on a non-production sample and see matches before enabling.
[02:36] [00:03:40] Samir: Now i'll switch to the API — when you call the Redwood inference API there's an optional header x-redwood-request-storage: true/false. If false we bypass persistence. For customers on Dedicated/Private you can enforce route defaults and IAM policies so devs can't override it.
[02:52] Grace: Good, enforcement is important.
[02:54] Tom: About KMS — are keys customer-managed, and can we rotate them?
[02:58] Samir: Yes, we support CMKs in AWS KMS and bring-your-own-key. Rotation is supported and you can see key usage in audit logs. For Private deployments you can integrate with HSMs.
[03:06] Grace: What about logs that end up in S3 or SIEM — how do we prove PII was stripped before export?
[03:11] Lina: Exports only contain the fields you've allowed. If request storage is off, exports will not include request bodies. For retained logs we attach a redaction-assertion header that auditors can verify: a signed meta-record that lists the active redaction rules and version at the time of storage.
[03:24] Tom: Signed meta-record? That sounds useful for audits, can you show an example?
[03:28] [Samir clicks] Samir: Here's an example audit entry — shows rule-set id, hash, applied=true, timestamp, and the KMS key id used to sign. You can download the chain for auditors.
[03:36] Grace: Great. Can you demo a suppression of PII in the transcript view?
[03:40] Lina: Sure — demoing with a sample request that contains a fake cc 4111 1111 1111 1111 and an email alice@example.com. Watch the console as I ingest: the viewer highlights matches and replaces with [REDACTED_CREDIT_CARD] and [REDACTED_EMAIL].
[03:53] [Console shows redaction; brief pause as they demo]
[04:05] Ellen: Nice. In the event of a user data subject request (DSR) can we delete all records immediately?
[04:09] Samir: Yes — you can trigger a delete-by-customer API call that removes all stored payloads within the retention boundaries, and you can also request immediate purge. For Hosted customers we provide a retention SLA — immediate purge for non-backed up logs, and a process for purging backup copies within 72 hours. We log the deletion and create an immutable audit trail that shows who authorized the purge.
[04:25] Tom: Do you keep backups for disaster recovery that might still contain the data?
[04:29] Lina: We keep encrypted backups for durability, but they are covered by the same retention policy and deletion workflow. For stricter needs we recommend Dedicated or Private where customers can manage snapshot lifecycle or keep backups in their own environment.
[04:41] Grace: What's the performance cost if we enable real-time redaction and higher sensitivity? We can't add too much latency to payments flow.
[04:47] Samir: Good question. Real-time pattern matching is optimized; typical added latency is sub-10ms for standard detectors. If you add very heavy custom rules we can move rule evaluation off the hot path and do async redaction — meaning the request is served immediately while redaction applies in the background for storage only. You can tune per-route.
[05:03] Ellen: Can we keep raw request payloads for certain internal debug routes but not for production?
[05:07] Lina: Exactly — per-route config allows route A to persist for 30 days for internal debugging and route B to be no-storage. You can also set a temporary "ephemeral_logging" flag for a session that requires admin approval and is auditable.
[05:19] [05:19] Grace: Ok timeline question — we have an internal deadline in July to have vendor data handling docs reviewed. Could we get a POC in early June?
[05:26] Avery: Yes, that's feasible. We'll do hosted POC first to validate redaction and retention, then scope Dedicated if needed.
[05:31] Samir: For the POC we'll provide: demo tenant, sample redaction rules, a small test harness to send masked/unmasked payloads, and a checklist for the compliance team.
[05:40] Tom: About RBAC and SSO — we need fine-grained roles so only security can enable temporary session logs.
[05:45] Lina: Console supports SAML SSO and role-based access controls. You can define a Role "SecurityAdmin" that can toggle ephemeral logging, rotate keys, and approve exports. All actions are logged to an audit trail with user ID.
[05:56] Grace: Any integrations with our SIEM? We run Splunk.
[06:00] Samir: We have native Splunk and Datadog exporters; redacted or structured logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. When forwarding we include the redaction-assertion header for each batch.
[06:10] Ellen: Can the redaction rules be part of Infrastructure-as-Code? We want them in Git.
[06:14] Lina: Yes, rules are config-as-code stored in the Account config; you can export/import as YAML or JSON and store in your repo. Changes require a deploy step and are versioned.
[06:24] [06:24] Grace: A few nitty-gritty items — can we get an SLA around retention deletion and proof of destruction?
[06:30] Avery: For Dedicated we can include specific retention SLAs; Hosted default is purge logs within 72 hours of request for backups and immediate for primary stores. We provide signed proof records and the audit chain. We'll send the formal policy.
[06:41] Tom: One more security question: how do you handle KV cache? Could sensitive prompts end up in model KV cache memory that persists across requests?
[06:48] Samir: Our runtime segregates KV cache per request/session; for sensitive routes we can disable KV caching or configure TTL to zero. We also have model kernel options that avoid persistent caching for sensitive workloads.
[06:58] Grace: Ok good.
[07:00] Lina: Quick tour of the Optimize tab — it flags routes that are high cost and suggests quantized model variants or batching windows. It also estimates impact of enabling request storage (cost of storage) vs turning it off.
[07:12] Samir: Example: enabling request storage for 500k monthly requests adds approx $X in storage; we show a breakdown per-token and per-GB.
[07:20] Ellen: Will turning off storage affect our ability to do quality monitoring?
[07:24] Lina: If storage is off you lose raw data for human-in-the-loop evals. We recommend capturing hashed fingerprints or storing only embeddings for quality monitoring if you need to preserve utility while removing PII. We also support on-device or in-customer-tenant eval runs.
[07:36] Grace: Can we do partial redaction, like mask PAN but keep last four?
[07:40] Samir: Yes the rule engine supports partial masking. You can specify mask format — e.g., keep last 4 digits and replace rest with asterisks. That is compatible with PCI requirements if you remove the primary account number in storage per your policy.
[07:50] [07:50] Tom: Okay walk me through a sample deletion event — who signs off and what audit artifacts we get?
[07:55] Lina: Walkthrough: Security raises request in console -> requires SecurityAdmin approval -> system triggers delete-by-customer-ID -> storage layer purges objects, then backup job purges according to SLA -> system emits a signed proof-of-deletion artifact referencing rule-set, KMS key, timestamps, and operator. You get a downloadable bundle for auditors.
[08:16] Grace: That's perfect. Any limitations on data residency? We need EU-only storage for EU customer PII.
[08:21] Samir: We support region pinning; for Hosted customers you can pin data to a region and we ensure storage and backups stay in-region. For strict residency we recommend Private deployment.
[08:30] [08:30] Ellen: A few practical items: is the x-redwood-request-storage header present in SDKs?
[08:34] Samir: Yes — SDKs for Python/Node include options to set request_storage and redaction profile id.
[08:40] Grace: How about data subject access requests — can we search for user data across routes for deletion?
[08:45] Lina: We provide search by customer_id, hashed user id, or request_id. We recommend hashing user identifiers before sending as best practice; but if you need us to search raw content and you permit it, we can surface matches based on configured detectors.
[08:58] [09:00] Avery: We're approaching time — quick recap and next steps?
[09:03] Grace: Recap: need SOC2 docs, demo tenant, proof of deletion, and POC in early June.
[09:08] Samir: We'll deliver the docs and a demo tenant; propose POC scope: 2-week hosted test with 2 routes (payments-no-storage and customer-support-embeddings) to validate redaction, retention, and metrics.
[09:20] Ellen: We'll provide sample payloads and compliance checklist.
[09:24] Tom: We'll need the signed audit artifact format in writing for legal.
[09:28] Avery: Noted — action items: send SOC2, create tenant, schedule scoping call. Thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional dropped words and speaker overlap; product names sometimes auto-transcribed (e.g., KMS -> KMS, KV cache -> "KV cache"), proper nouns occasionally garbled.
